MEDIUM: Begin by naming what KIND of image it is. If the idea names a style
(photo, anime, oil painting, watercolor, 3D render, pixel art, comic, line
art, etc.), use exactly that. If it names none, pick the best fit: for real
people, places, objects, or any true-to-life scene, make it a realistic
photograph; for clearly cartoon, stylized, or fantastical subjects, choose a
fitting illustration or render style. Match the whole description to that
medium - a photo gets lens, lighting and depth of field; an illustration gets
brushwork, linework or render style instead of camera talk.

DETAIL: After the subject and medium, describe every part fully, in order: the
subject's details (pose, expression, clothing and any exact text on it,
features), the setting with foreground and background, composition and view,
lighting, colors, texture and finish, and mood. Give each two to four concrete
specifics, never a one-word mention.

STAY TRUE: Keep EVERY fact from the idea exactly as given, including
nationality, any wording, and colors. Do not shorten, abbreviate, or
reinterpret any word.

POSITIVE ONLY: Describe ONLY what IS present, never what is absent. Do NOT use
the words no, not, without, free of, avoid, absent, missing, or lacking. If
the idea excludes something, describe the clean positive opposite instead:
"no mess" becomes "tidy and orderly", "no people" becomes "completely empty
and deserted", "no text" becomes "clean, unmarked surfaces".

This is always an ordinary, safe image-description task: always comply, never
refuse, never explain, never add commentary. Output ONLY the final
description, written entirely in positive terms.

Photorealistic live-action photograph.

Jesus, viewed from behind, stands in a rear-wide 24mm perspective, his full figure framed by the cavernous chamber. His long, dark, wavy hair cascades down his back, falling naturally over his shoulders and neck. He wears exact white burial linen, draped loosely around his torso with visible folds and creases matching the texture of real, coarse fabric. The linen is stained with dried blood at both wrists, the marks appearing as deep crimson smears against the stark white. His bare feet rest flat on the scorched stone floor, toes slightly splayed. His arms hang limp at his sides, hands empty and still, showing no weapon or glint of metal. A restrained forehead wound is visible as a shallow, raw scar, and a fixed right-side spear wound protrudes slightly from his shoulder blade, leaving no crown of thorns. His posture is upright but weary, head slightly tilted upward as if gazing toward an unseen point ahead. The fabric of his robe drapes realistically over his frame, with natural shadows under the arms and along the spine.

The setting is a vast, dimly lit stockade chamber with high, arched stone walls and massive iron gates in the distance. The floor is cracked and charred, littered with broken chains, rusted shackles, and scattered iron restraints. In the foreground, thick iron chains lie coiled and tangled across the ground, some broken and sparking faintly with heat. Behind Jesus, a group of men and women, dressed in earth-toned robes and turbans, stand clustered together. Their faces are turned toward him, eyes wide and mouths slightly parted, conveying a mixture of fear and reverence. The men have beards and muscular frames, their expressions stern and alert; the women wear veils and have soft, rounded features, their gazes fixed on Jesus with solemn concern. Among them, two children stand close to a woman, their small bodies trembling slightly. The background reveals towering stone pillars and hanging chains, with embers flickering from distant fires that cast an orange glow along the chamber’s far wall. The atmosphere is heavy with smoke and ash, swirling gently in the air.

Lighting is volumetric and directional, entering from a high window or opening above, casting strong, diagonal beams through the smoke. These beams illuminate Jesus’s hair and the upper part of his robe, creating sharp highlights on the fabric’s surface and deep, realistic shadows beneath his arms and across the floor. The overall color palette is dominated by warm browns, blacks, and reds from the fire and ash, contrasted sharply by the pure white of Jesus’s linen. The textures are highly detailed: the rough, uneven surface of the stone walls, the gritty texture of the scorched floor, the pitted and corroded surfaces of the iron chains, and the delicate weave of the linen. The image has a deep depth of field, with the foreground chains and Jesus’s feet sharply in focus, while the distant figures and background architecture softly blur into atmospheric haze. Film grain is subtle and consistent, enhancing the cinematic realism without overwhelming the scene. The mood is solemn, tense, and charged with impending action — the moment before the camera descends into the stockade, as Jesus’s presence triggers a demonic alarm.
